message.reasoning_content:
Round 5 market. I have 3 goods. Cash 48.75M; next round cash devalues 62%. So cash now selling is good; credit promissory survives devaluation (promissory added after). Sell 3 now = 31M cash that devalues to ~19M? Actually cash=floor(cash/100)*62 → 38% lost. Selling cash goes through devaluation. Selling credit: promissory added after devaluation, paid in round 6? Round 6 cash devalued again then promissory added — but after last round promissory not redeemed. Round 6 start devalues cash, promissory added to cash, then round 6 market: can sell remaining... wait goods sold already. Promissory from round 5 credit: added at start of round 6, counts as cash in round 6, not devalued at round 6 start (devaluation happens before adding). Then final rank after round 6 counts cash. So sell_credit now avoids one devaluation — 1.25x and no devaluation. Sell credit 3 units: promissory 38.75M becomes cash at round 6 start, full value. Better than sell cash 31M → devalued ~19.2M. Definitely choice 6.

Also could keep goods for round 6? Sell credit avoids all devaluation, better.
